Subject: Dedicated capacity MAP orchestration & stakeholder roster

Hi Hanna / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our recap, Acme ML is evaluating a dedicated GPU pool for inference of your production recommendation model. To keep momentum I wanted to propose a lightweight Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to align owners, milestones, and throughput targets so we can get a deterministic close and an initial provisioning runbook.

High-level proposal (please comment):
- Goal: Production-ready Dedicated pool in your VPC (or Redwood-hosted dedicated) supporting the recommender at target SLA.
- Evaluation window: 3 weeks (staging + canary) leading into a 2-week ramp to steady state.
- Throughput targets: baseline 350 requests/min sustained with p95 < 300ms for 512-token median request; peak burst to 1,200 requests/min.
- Initial pool suggestion: 4x A100-80GB for inference (horizontal scaling allowed), autoscale policy +2 nodes for burst.
- Success criteria: p95 latency <300ms, error rate <1%, cost per 1k requests within agreed threshold.

Proposed owners (please confirm or update):
- Customer lead (Acme): Hanna Li — technical contact / evaluation sign-off
- Procurement (Acme): Tom Brooks / procurement@acme-ml.com — commercial & PO
- Redwood: Diego Fernandez — MAP owner & program lead
- Redwood infra lead: Rishi Malhotra — capacity config & provisioning
- Redwood onboarding / CS: Marissa Cole — runbooks & training
- Redwood observability: Grace O'Connor — dashboards / alerts
- Redwood rollout ops: Jordan Blake — canary/rollout policy

Attachments: Redwood MAP template (redwood_dedicated_map_v1.pdf) and a short checklist. I also dropped a shared Drive link to the MAP doc in related_links.

Requested next steps:
1) Hanna / Tom: confirm owners + any additional stakeholders (security, legal) by EOD Friday.
2) We'll book a 60-min kickoff to walk through MAP, allocate tasks, and lock the evaluation dates.
3) Rishi / Marissa: sketch an initial pool config and provisioning ETA.

Availability: proposing Tue 7/6 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 7/7 8:00-9:00 PT — happy to adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

—
Diego Fernandez

Diego / team —

Thanks for the write-up. Quick technical clarifications and an initial provisioning plan from infra:

Clarifications:
- KV cache: we support persistent KV cache within a dedicated node family if the pool is configured with sticky assignment + persistent volume for KV. We'll document warm-start guarantees in the MAP.
- Node sizing: 4x A100-80GB is a sensible starting point for performance headroom. A 6x A100-40GB alternative reduces per-node risk (fewer OOM/evictions) and improves rolling updates. I'll include both cost estimates in the MAP.

Initial provisioning timeline (tentative):
- Day 0-2: Networking & IAM (VPC peering / transit setup) — dependency: Acme infra.
- Day 3-5: Provision base pool (4 nodes), install runtime & model artifacts.
- Day 6-8: Staging validation, traffic shaping, KV warm-up script run.
- Day 9-14: Canary with a 5-10% slice of prod traffic, monitoring + rollback playbook.

Autoscale policy: target CPU/GPU utilization 65-75% with burst +2 nodes at 85% sustained for >30s.

I'll prepare a short appendix for the MAP with: node configs, expected p95 based on our previous runs, costs for both node mixes, and a checklist of required firewall rules for port ranges.

I'll be on the kickoff Tue 7/6 10:00 PT.

-rishi
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
